rows.heard: Long ago, the world was a lit hall. The Lanternwrights, who kept its lamps, called it Halcyre.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: They held its wild magic still with one great working, the Song.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Then the song broke. Nobody alive knows why. The lamps went out, one by one.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: The magic spilled. Now it moves over the open land like weather, and people call it the Drift.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Glimmer, that turns the lamps blue. The gray that makes a village forget itself. Hollowwind, Brightfall.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: So people live inside wards, small villages gathered round the old stones that still hum. Every village is a lamp in a large dark room.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: This is Hearthvale, a kettle fire that has never once gone out, and a singing stone at the bottom of the well, the Wellstone.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Every household keeps one flame on the Chapel Altar, and the flames hold the ward up.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: 25 winters ago for 11 still nights, light fell on the valley like snow.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: By midsummer, old Hobb the Lamplighter and Wenna the Beekeeper, long past hope of children, had a daughter. They named her for a star, Lyra.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: The old women counted on their fingers and said nothing out loud.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Maren Ashgrove, the village's wardrite, taught her magic for 13 years.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Three months ago on Lyra's birthday, Maren went over the wall of the Sunken Ruins with a Lantern and a rope and did not come back.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Maren's notes called the stone ring on the Hollowcrown the other end. Lyra paid Hess the boardrunner to take her up.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: If she went anywhere, she went up there.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Mmm, then we climb.
rows.speaker: hess

rows.heard: At dawn they reached the crown ring, nine broken stones in the snow.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: In the middle, the snow had melted in a perfect circle. No footprints in, none out.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: And in it lay someone, warm, breathing, a sword beside them.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Lyra.
rows.speaker: hess

rows.heard: Lyra, it isn't her.
rows.speaker: hess

rows.heard: I know, I know.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: We bind their hands loosely.
rows.speaker: hess

rows.heard: Loosely, we're not leaving a living person up here.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: It was you.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: They carried you down on a litter made of Lyra's cloak. When you passed the well, the Wellstone hummed for the whole square to hear.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: You slept in the chapel for 81 nights. Six days ago you woke, remembering nothing.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Two days ago, on the King's Road, wolves came at dusk. You stood beside her.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Morning. Still breathing? Good. I'd hate to have carried you down a mountain for nothing.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: In case the mountain took this too, I'm Lyra Ambrel. This is the Wayhouse in Hearthvale.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: I hold your key. That's the Hearthwatch. I look in, I sleep in the spare bed when I feel like it, and the Moot pays me.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Nobody's obliged to keep one. I took yours because I wanted to.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Now! Breakfast at the Kettle, and you tell me if anything's come back. Even something small?
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Who's that? Come here, let me hear you.
rows.speaker: wenna

rows.heard: Ma 'am, it's the one off the mountain. You asked to meet them.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: I did. My eyes are no use past my own hand, so you'll have to bend down. Hold still.
rows.speaker: wenna

rows.heard: Her hands are cool and dry and smell of beeswax. She reads your face the way she reads her hives, slowly and missing nothing.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Hmm, young, tired, not a liar's jaw.
rows.speaker: wenna

rows.heard: The mountain gives, and the mountain takes, and it never gives for nothing. Mind, you're worth what it took.
rows.speaker: wenna

rows.heard: Well, now, look who's up and walking.
rows.speaker: hobb

rows.heard: Everyone found deserves a lamp. I hung one by your door. Mind the cat doesn't sit in it.
rows.speaker: hobb

rows.heard: Da, your spectacles are on your head.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Are they? Well now. So they are.
rows.speaker: hobb

rows.heard: Bring them to supper, Lyra Ambrel. I want to hear them eat.
rows.speaker: wenna

rows.heard: Thirty -eight flames burn on the altar, one for every household under the ward.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: As you come near, every one of them leans towards you, the way a flower leans to a window.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: They do that. They did it every night you slept here, child.
rows.speaker: aveline

rows.heard: A question someone has sent us. I have not found the answer. I have stopped minding.
rows.speaker: aveline

rows.heard: Don't look at me. I don't know why either. I've asked them.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: You keep watching my hands when I light a lamp. Wanna know how it started? It's a short one.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Long Watch Night. I was 11. A hollow wind came down off the crownfells and blew out every lamp on the square at once.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: It knocked Daa off his ladder onto the ice.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: I was so frightened and so angry and so cold that I lit them, all of them, at the same moment, in violet.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: One burst. Dass sat up on the ice and said, Well, now.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: And Maren came out of the kettle in her nightgown, looked at the lamps, looked at me, and said,
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Well, there goes my quiet old age.
rows.speaker: maren

rows.heard: She took me on the next morning. I've been cold ever since. Worth it.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: See the iron in the North Face? Bram's Steaks, the Moot sealed it five years ago. Because of me.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Davin wanted coin for the Saltmere Roadguard. The crystals in the cut were the quickest coin in the valley. He asked me to come. A mage would make it safe.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: I could feel it stirring. I said no. He asked again. And again, sweetly. He talked about the sea.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: So I said yes, not because I'd changed my mind, because I didn't want to be the one who made his life small.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: It woke around us. Slimes out of the walls? Something with too many bones. I cast until I guttered.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: David ran. For help, he said. Brynn dragged me out on her back, and in the last passage, the stone came down on her leg.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: I lent warmth into it for three nights. It wasn't enough. She walks with a stick now in Saltmere. She forgave me years ago.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Maren didn't shout, she said.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: You spent your judgment like a coin you didn't have. Never again go where you've already said no. For anyone. Not for him. Not for me.
rows.speaker: maren

rows.heard: So when I say no, that's why, it isn't about you, it's about the coin.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Sister, tell them what you saw at Midsummer.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: I saw her go, child, dusk on the longest day, her gray cloak, a lantern, a coil of rope over her shoulder.
rows.speaker: aveline

rows.heard: She walked down the road toward the marsh as if she were late for supper. I called after her.
rows.speaker: aveline

rows.heard: She raised her hand. She did not turn around.
rows.speaker: aveline

rows.heard: The blue lights began that night. I have prayed for her every dusk since. Prayer is mostly waiting, and waiting I can do.
rows.speaker: aveline

rows.heard: She paid a month ahead at the kettle. She bought turnips for a long walk. People who mean to die don't buy turnips.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: This is as close as the Moot lets anyone come, sealed by order of the chapel 110 years ago.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: She didn't use the gate, she went over the low stretch of wall on the marsh side, it slumped into the marsh the same night.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: I climbed the highwall once, alone, on Hess's rope, something with no skin got hold of my boot.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: I'm not going in again without the key. A gate's a way out. You can run through. A rope isn't.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: The bandits have the key, so that is where it starts, if it starts.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: If someone comes out, I hope whoever it is is kind.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: That's her hand. She wrote it before she went through.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Someone did come out at the other end, lying warm in the snow with a sword.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Well, you'd better be kind then.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Wait, wait, what was that?
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Light gathers between your hands out of nothing, no flame, no breath spent. For a heartbeat, there are marks in it, sharp little shapes, there and gone.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: That isn't a spark. I make sparks. I know what they cost me, everyone.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Those marks. Maren used to copy marks like that off the Ruins Wall by candlelight. Lanternwright letters.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Wicks and Ashes. Right. Breathe, Lyra.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Do that again, slowly, not at me.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: You open your hand before the altar, and the light comes.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Thirty -eight flames stand up tall, everyone, and bend towards you like flowers to a window.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: There, I sat 81 nights wondering what they would do. Now I know, and I understand it less.
rows.speaker: aveline

rows.heard: They've never done that for me. Not once. I'm not jealous. I'm a little jealous.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: That's far enough. The toll's paid at the fork, not up here.
rows.speaker: varek

rows.heard: He winds up before he swings. Watch his shoulders and move.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: And nobody dies on this hill, not even him.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Brave. Come on, then. Let's see what Hearthvale sends up a hill.
rows.speaker: varek

rows.heard: The wood goes quiet, then every wolf in Whisperwood answers one voice.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Greyjaw. Hess has been tracking him since spring. He's why the packs come so close.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: When he crouches, he's coming. Step aside, not back.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: In the deepest rain pool, something vast and pink stirs, and every little slime in the quarry turns to look at you.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: That's not a slime, that's a lot of slimes that agreed on something.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Hit it hard and it splits. Kill the little ones before it drinks them back.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Mirror Lake goes still as glass, then it hums, low, from somewhere under the boards.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Hmm. Never heard her hum that loud. Mind the edges.
rows.speaker: corran

rows.heard: Still water that sits too long stirs, that's the old saying, nobody set a whole lake.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: It has to come up to hit us. When it does, so do we.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: In the lower hall, the cold light gathers into a lantern, and the lantern lifts.
rows.speaker: narrator

rows.heard: Gravelight. Every Moot in the lowmarch forbids it and here it is, walking.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: That Lantern, like the statue upstairs? Maren carried a Miner's Lantern in here. Hers burned yellow.
rows.speaker: lyra

rows.heard: Its shield won't take a plain cut. Hit it with something heavy or with light.
rows.speaker: lyra
